A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MesaNet. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model evaluations, MAD and RegBench experiments, parity experiments, and CG-step analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds needle-in-a-haystack evaluations, full-model inference-throughput measurements, and an original-Mesa comparison.

M1.justification: The gated two-state recurrence, regularized least-squares readout, CG solver, chunkwise computation and Hawk-Mesa architecture remain unchanged. Expanded derivations and precision disclosures do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix L.3 adds RULER single-needle retrieval using noise and essay haystacks with word, number and UUID key/value formats. Existing language, synthetic and parity task coverage is retained; MAD and RegBench are relocated.

E2.justification: v2 Section 4 adds an empirical comparison with the original sequential Mesa layer at approximately 400M parameters. The decoding-throughput comparison also includes Gated DeltaNet, absent from v1's single-layer inference panel. Existing language and synthetic benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new NIAH protocol evaluates 1B models trained on 50B tokens at lengths 2048 and 4096, with 1000 samples per setting. New full-model decoding measurements sweep batch size and generation length on H100 and TPUv5. Existing training budgets and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds retrieval sensitivity analysis across haystack and key/value types, plus full-model throughput scaling across batch sizes, lengths and CG counts. Existing CG ablations, parity experiments, token-position analyses and internal-state analyses remain; redisplaying the CG analysis adds no new ablation.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6 specifies averaging timing measurements over five iterations. Table 19 reports mean and standard deviation across nine key/value combinations, measuring condition variability rather than training-seed uncertainty. Existing uncertainty reporting over ten randomly selected few-shot prefixes is unchanged.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark values are unchanged. Additions include full-model throughput, the original-Mesa comparison, and NIAH scores: MesaNet obtains 99.5 ± 0.5% and 95.1 ± 3.9% on noise haystacks at lengths 2048 and 4096, respectively. These are newly reported results, not improvements over matching v1 measurements; v1's single-layer inference curve is removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands the formal treatment of related learning rules, including LongHorn and Atlas objectives and updates. v2 also corrects the regularizer from Tr(Phi^T Lambda Phi) to Tr(Phi Lambda Phi^T) and adds a stationarity derivation and uniqueness justification for Mesa's solution in Appendix D, where v1 mainly asserted the equivalence.

C1.justification: v2 drops the introduction's explicit priority claim that MesaNet is the first linearized transformer to match transformers on RegBench; matching performance remains reported in Appendix K. The central claims about parallelizable optimal test-time training, language modeling and dynamic computation are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds a memory-bound decoding explanation for competitive throughput despite higher FLOPs, cautions that lower-precision CG convergence remains insufficiently investigated, and qualifies essay-haystack conclusions because scores vary substantially across formats. Existing long-context and finite-memory limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G.5 newly specifies FP32 matrix multiplication inside the Pallas CG kernel with BF16 input/output handling. A reproducibility statement replaces v1's explicit Mesa implementation availability statement with a future-release promise, although framework links remain. This changes the documented access information without establishing actual repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning Lattice, Trellis, Zoology, RULER and Muon. It also refines v1's description of Atlas as exactly a sliding-window Mesa variant by acknowledging nonlinear memory and different optimization updates. The central positioning relative to the original Mesa layer is retained.

P1.justification: Synthetic experiments move from the main text to Appendix K; the appendix contents list disappears and a reproducibility statement is added. Contributions and method explanations receive localized revisions, alongside author, header and citation-style changes. Most existing prose and arguments are retained.

P2.justification: Several central displays are reorganized: v1 Figure 6's grouped bar charts become v2 Table 3, the recurrence overview moves into the main text, and synthetic displays move to the appendix. Figure 2 loses its inference panel. New objective and NIAH tables and a four-panel throughput figure are added; the CG analysis is duplicated as Figures 5 and 7.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical auditability through the corrected regularizer and explicit derivation, supplies useful solver-precision details, and strengthens practical evaluation with full-model timing and controlled retrieval tests. The core empirical findings remain stable. Less clear code-release wording and duplicated CG figures partly offset these incremental benefits.
